- **Q: Can LokalBot transcribe an existing audio file?** Yes. Import an audio or video file from the Meetings list, or drop it on the list, and LokalBot transcribes and summarizes it like a meeting it recorded. It has no subtitle export; for subtitle files or batch transcription, MacWhisper is the better tool: and the two apps run fine side by side.
- **Q: Which one is more private?** Both can transcribe entirely on your Mac. The difference is in what surrounds it: LokalBot's summaries run on a built-in local model by default, and its source code is public under GPLv3, so you can check what it does with your audio.
- **Q: Do they use the same speech models?** Partly. Both can run Whisper-family models on your Mac. LokalBot defaults to Qwen3-ASR and also offers Parakeet and Granite Speech; the benchmarks page compares several of them on the same test set.

### LokalBot vs Superwhisper (https://www.lokalbot.com/lokalbot-vs-superwhisper · verified 2026-10-26)

Superwhisper started as a dictation app and is now a cross-platform voice tool: custom modes, AI rewrites, meeting recording, and apps for Mac, Windows, iOS, and Android. If voice-to-text is your main job, it goes deeper than LokalBot. LokalBot's dictation is simpler by design: hold ⌥ Space (Alt+Space on Windows and Linux), speak, it types: and it comes inside a free, open-source desktop app that also writes meeting notes, tracks your day, and autocompletes your writing.

| Feature | LokalBot | Superwhisper |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Dictation | Hold or toggle ⌥ Space (Alt+Space on Windows and Linux), live transcript pill, pastes at the cursor | Deeper: custom modes, AI text processing, per-app behavior |
| Where speech runs | On your computer: fine-tuned Qwen3-ASR by default (v3 1.7B on Mac, v1 0.6B compact), with Parakeet and Whisper as alternatives, plus Granite Speech on Mac | Local models such as Whisper and Cohere Transcribe, with optional cloud models |
| Cloud path | None by default; remote inference only for servers you approve | Optional cloud models and AI processing |
| Dictation audio | Scratch recording deleted after transcription by default | Kept by default; Settings sets how long recordings stay |
| Meeting notes | Bot-free microphone + system-audio capture, local summaries, searchable library | On Mac: bot-free meeting recording with speaker labels and automatic summaries |
| Day timeline | App and window activity by default; screen text and encrypted screenshots are opt-in and deleted after 14 days | No |
| Writing autocomplete | Cotyping ghost text as you type | No: AI modes transform what you dictate instead |
| Source code | Open source, GPLv3 | Proprietary |
| Price | Free: dictation included, nothing gated | Free tier · Pro $8.49/mo, with yearly and lifetime options |
| Platforms | macOS 15+ on Apple Silicon; Windows 10/11 x64 and Linux x86_64 in alpha; iOS and Android companion apps | macOS, Windows, iOS, and Android |

- **Q: Which speech models does LokalBot use?** On Mac, Qwen3-ASR 1.7B by default, with Parakeet, Granite Speech, and Whisper large-v3 turbo as alternatives. On Windows and Linux, Qwen3-ASR 0.6B by default, with Parakeet, SenseVoice, GigaAM for Russian, and Whisper turbo. All of them run on your computer. Dictation reuses the engine and language you picked for meetings and keeps it warm, so transcription starts as soon as you hold the key.
- **Q: Does LokalBot keep my dictation audio?** No. On Mac, by default it records to a scratch file, transcribes it on-device, pastes the text, deletes the recording, and even pauses your music before it starts listening. On Windows and Linux the audio stays in memory unless you turn on Keep dictation audio files.
- **Q: Can I run both apps?** Sure: they use different shortcuts. Some people will want Superwhisper for heavy dictation workflows and LokalBot for meetings and everything else. LokalBot is free, so trying the combination costs nothing.

### LokalBot vs Wispr Flow (https://www.lokalbot.com/lokalbot-vs-wispr-flow · verified 2026-11-26)

Wispr Flow is a popular cloud dictation app across Mac, Windows, iPhone, and Android, and its Notetaker records calls without a bot. Both features run in Wispr's cloud under a paid account. LokalBot is a free, open-source (GPLv3) alternative that runs dictation and bot-free meeting notes on your computer by default, adds a day timeline and 56 ms autocomplete, and natively imports your existing Wispr Flow meetings and personal dictionary directly from flow.sqlite with zero network calls.

| Feature | LokalBot | Wispr Flow |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Where speech runs | On your computer: fine-tuned Qwen3-ASR by default (v3 1.7B on Mac, v1 0.6B compact), with Parakeet and Whisper as alternatives, plus Granite Speech on Mac | Wispr's cloud; there is no on-device mode |
| Works offline | After a one-time model download | Needs a connection |
| Account required | None | Yes |
| Migration from Wispr Flow | Reads flow.sqlite read-only to import meetings and personal dictionary words (skipping snippets and deleted entries) | N/A |
| Dictation | Hold or toggle ⌥ Space (Alt+Space on Windows/Linux), fine-tuned Qwen3-ASR with 100% vocab recall and 0 silence hallucinations | Deeper: AI cleanup, personal dictionary, snippets, per-app styles, and command mode |
| Meeting capture | Bot-free microphone + system audio; detects meetings and, on a fresh install, asks before recording | Bot-free Notetaker for Zoom, Meet, Teams, Slack huddles, and more |
| Ask across meetings | Cited answers from a local model that link back to the transcript and audio | Answers across your meeting history, linked to the moment they came from |
| Where meetings are kept | On your computer: audio, transcripts, and notes | Transcripts in Wispr's cloud for cross-device sync, with configurable retention |
| Transcription languages | On Mac: 52 languages and dialects with the default model; 99 with Whisper | Dictation: 100+ · Notetaker: 21 |
| Connect AI tools | Read-only CLI and MCP server, off until you turn them on in Settings | MCP for Claude, ChatGPT, and Gemini |
| Compliance | No LokalBot server ever holds your dictation or meetings | SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001, and HIPAA-ready plans |
| Day timeline | App and window activity by default; screen text and encrypted screenshots are opt-in and deleted after 14 days | No |
| Writing autocomplete | Cotyping (Gemma 4 E2B LokalBot v4), in almost any app (on Linux: X11, or Wayland on Sway, Hyprland, GNOME, and KDE Plasma) | No; AI edits what you dictate instead |
| Source code | Open source, GPLv3 | Proprietary |
| Price | Free: dictation and meeting notes included, nothing gated | Free: 2,000 dictated words a week and a weekly meeting cap · Pro $15/mo ($12 annual) · Growth $23/mo ($18 annual) · Enterprise custom |
| Platforms | macOS 15+ on Apple Silicon; Windows 10/11 x64 and Linux x86_64 in alpha; iOS and Android companion apps | Dictation: Mac, Windows, iOS, and Android · Notetaker: Mac and Windows |

- **Q: Can I import my Wispr Flow meetings and personal dictionary into LokalBot?** Yes. On Mac, Recording > Import Meetings From reads Wispr Flow's meetings table and transcript files from your local flow.sqlite database read-only, without touching dictation history, audio, or screenshots. Settings > Models > Transcribe > Advanced > Language & vocabulary > Import from Wispr Flow imports your custom dictionary words (skipping snippets and deleted entries) with zero network requests.
- **Q: Does Wispr Flow have an offline or on-device mode?** No. Wispr's data-controls page states that transcription always happens in its cloud, and Notetaker transcripts are stored there for cross-device sync. LokalBot transcribes dictation and meetings on your computer after a one-time model download, and keeps working without a connection.
- **Q: Is LokalBot's dictation as good as Wispr Flow's?** Test both on your own voice. Wispr Flow goes further on cloud prose editing, snippets, and per-app tone rewrites. LokalBot 0.14.0 ships fine-tuned Qwen3-ASR 1.7B (v3) with 100% custom vocabulary recall, 0 silence hallucinations, and automatic spacing/capitalization cleanup before pasting, all running offline on the same speech model used for meetings.
- **Q: Can I use both?** Yes. They use different shortcuts, and LokalBot is free. Some people keep Wispr Flow for heavy phone dictation and use LokalBot for meetings they prefer not to upload, offline dictation, a searchable day timeline, and autocomplete.

### LokalBot vs Cotypist (https://www.lokalbot.com/lokalbot-vs-cotypist · verified 2026-11-26)

Cotypist (cotypist.app) is a polished proprietary macOS app that brings local, offline ghost-text autocomplete to Apple Silicon using on-device Gemma and Qwen models, with a 100-word daily free cap and Plus/Pro subscriptions (~$72-$108/yr). LokalBot ships free, unlimited open-source inline autocomplete across macOS, Windows, and Linux (alpha) using our Apache-2.0 fine-tuned Gemma 4 E2B (LokalBot v4) model (56 ms typing median, 20.2 ms boundary median, 49-53 ms after a 5-minute pause, and 56/56 context grounding), plus optional grounding in your own meeting notes.

| Feature | LokalBot | Cotypist |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Where autocomplete runs | 100% on-device via in-process llama.cpp (Gemma 4 E2B LokalBot v4 Q6_K or LFM2.5 1.2B) | 100% on-device on Apple Silicon (Gemma / Qwen local models) |
| Measured latency (M4 Max) | 56 ms typing median (20.2 ms boundary, 49-53 ms after 5-min idle warm-up) | Advertised low-latency inline suggestions and fast resume |
| Knows your meeting notes | Opt-in: pulls up to 2 relevant facts from your own meetings (56/56 grounding benchmark) | No meeting library |
| Window context privacy | Reads accessibility text above the field; private browser windows and password fields excluded | Clipboard awareness and per-app custom instructions on Pro |
| Free usage limits | Unlimited, free forever | Free: 100 accepted words/day (30-day Pro trial) |
| Also included in the app | Bot-free meeting notes, dictation, semantic search, day timeline, read-only MCP | Autocomplete and autocorrect only |
| Source code | Open source (GPLv3; Cotabby autocomplete files AGPLv3) | Proprietary |
| Price | Free | Free (100 words/day) · Plus ~$6-$8/mo (~$72/yr, 1 Mac) · Pro ~$9-$12/mo (~$108/yr, 3 Macs, larger models) |
| Platforms | macOS 15+ on Apple Silicon; Windows 10/11 x64 and Linux x86_64 in alpha; iOS and Android companion apps | macOS 14+ on Apple Silicon only (no Windows or Linux) |

- **Q: How fast is LokalBot's autocomplete compared to Cotypist?** In our reproducible headless keystroke benchmark on an Apple M4 Max, Gemma 4 E2B runs at 56 ms median while typing (20.2 ms median boundary latency and 80.0 ms p95 on LokalBot v4) and 49-53 ms on the first suggestion after a 5-minute idle pause. The Lightweight preset (LFM2.5 1.2B, 0.73 GB) hits 26 ms median. Full scripts and logs are on the benchmarks page.
- **Q: Does LokalBot send keystrokes to a cloud server?** No. Built-in autocomplete runs entirely in-process via llama.cpp on your computer, never reads password or credential fields, ignores private browser windows, and lets you exclude any app in Settings.
- **Q: Does LokalBot autocomplete work on Windows and Linux too?** Yes. The native Rust + GPUI app (alpha) runs the same Gemma 4 E2B and LFM2.5 1.2B models on Windows (via UI Automation) and Linux (X11, plus Wayland input-method support on Sway, Hyprland, GNOME, and KDE Plasma).

### LokalBot vs Handy, VoiceInk &amp; Voicenotes (https://www.lokalbot.com/lokalbot-vs-handy · verified 2026-11-26)

People searching for an open-source Wispr Flow replacement usually land on three distinct tools: Handy (MIT, free cross-platform Tauri push-to-talk dictation), VoiceInk (GPLv3 macOS and iOS dictation, free to compile or $25-$49 one-time for signed binaries), and Voicenotes (proprietary cloud voice-memo and meeting app at ~$99.99/yr). LokalBot sits beside Handy and VoiceInk as a free, open-source GPLv3 app with zero-hallucination local dictation, then adds bot-free two-track meeting notes, diarization, semantic search, 56 ms autocomplete, and local MCP in one memory budget.

| Feature | LokalBot | Handy / VoiceInk / Voicenotes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Where speech runs | On your computer: fine-tuned Qwen3-ASR by default (v3 1.7B on Mac, v1 0.6B compact), with Parakeet and Whisper as alternatives, plus Granite Speech on Mac | Handy & VoiceInk: local Whisper / Parakeet (VoiceInk also supports cloud APIs) · Voicenotes: cloud |
| Silence & vocab accuracy | Fine-tuned Qwen3-ASR 1.7B v3: 100% clean silence (0 ghosts), 100% custom vocab recall | Stock Whisper / Parakeet models (Handy uses Silero VAD; VoiceInk supports custom vocab/modes) |
| Bot-free meeting notes | Two-track capture, speaker diarization, local Qwen3.5 4B v4 summaries, citations | Handy: no · VoiceInk: audio transcription focus · Voicenotes: cloud meeting notes & voice memos |
| Search & Ask across history | 39 ms SQLite FTS5 + EmbeddingGemma 2 hybrid search, cited local Ask | Handy: no library · VoiceInk: transcript history · Voicenotes: cloud Ask AI second brain |
| Connect AI tools (MCP) | Read-only CLI and MCP server, off until you turn them on in Settings | None built in as a local meeting-library MCP server |
| Writing autocomplete & timeline | 56 ms Gemma 4 E2B autocomplete + opt-in day timeline | No |
| Source code & license | Open source, GPLv3 (free signed binaries on Mac, Win/Linux alpha) | Handy: MIT (free) · VoiceInk: GPLv3 ($25-$49 prebuilt Mac app) · Voicenotes: proprietary |
| Price | Free | Handy: Free · VoiceInk: $25-$49 one-time (free from source) · Voicenotes: Free (100 min/wk, 30d history) / ~$99.99/yr Pro |
| Platforms | macOS 15+ on Apple Silicon; Windows 10/11 x64 and Linux x86_64 in alpha; iOS and Android companion apps | Handy: Mac (ARM/Intel), Win, Linux · VoiceInk: macOS, iOS · Voicenotes: Web, Mac, Win, iOS, Android, Watch |

- **Q: How does LokalBot compare directly to Handy?** Handy (github.com/cjpais/Handy) is a great, minimal MIT-licensed push-to-talk dictation app that works on macOS (including Intel), Windows, and Linux. Handy stops at pasting dictated text. LokalBot adds bot-free two-track meeting recording, speaker diarization, local summaries, semantic search, Obsidian export, autocomplete, and a read-only MCP server.
- **Q: Why use LokalBot instead of VoiceInk on Mac?** Both are GPLv3 and run local speech models on Apple Silicon. VoiceInk sells signed binaries ($25-$49) and focuses deeply on dictation modes and prompt rewrites. LokalBot ships free signed and notarized Mac builds, fine-tuned Qwen3-ASR models that eliminate silence prompt echoes, and full meeting memory and coding-agent MCP.
- **Q: Can LokalBot replace Voicenotes for quick thoughts on a phone?** LokalBot's free iOS and Android companion apps record audio offline and sync end-to-end encrypted over LAN or Tailscale to your computer for local transcription and search. Voicenotes is better if you want standalone cloud transcription on a smartwatch without a home computer.

### LokalBot vs Screenpipe (https://www.lokalbot.com/lokalbot-vs-screenpipe · verified 2026-10-26)

Screenpipe records your screen and audio continuously and turns that history into context for any AI, through a local API and MCP server. It runs on macOS, Windows, and Linux. LokalBot starts smaller: it logs app and window activity by default, adds screen text and encrypted screenshots only if you opt in, and pairs that with bot-free meeting notes. The licenses differ too: LokalBot is GPLv3 open source, while Screenpipe's source is available under a commercial license.

| Feature | LokalBot | Screenpipe |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Captured by default | App name and window title; screen text and screenshots are opt-in | Screen, audio, and meetings, continuously |
| Retention and disk | Screenshots and extracted text deleted after 14 days by default | About 30 GB per month, with configurable retention |
| Meeting notes | Bot-free microphone + system-audio capture, local summaries, searchable library | Transcription with speaker identification; a meeting-summary pipe writes notes |
| Built-in AI | llama.cpp summaries and chat, no setup | Brings your history to the AI you already use |
| Connect AI tools | Read-only CLI and MCP server, off until you turn them on in Settings | Local REST API, MCP server, and agent pipes that can take actions |
| Encryption at rest | Screenshots are encrypted | Optional |
| Account required | None | Not for the core app |
| License | Open source, GPLv3 | Source-available under the Screenpipe Commercial License |
| Price | Free | Free (limited history) · Basic $21/mo or $250/yr · Business $42/seat/mo · Enterprise custom |
| Platforms | macOS 15+ on Apple Silicon; Windows 10/11 x64 and Linux x86_64 in alpha; iOS and Android companion apps | macOS 13+, Windows 10+, and Linux |

- **Q: Isn't Screenpipe open source?** It used to be MIT-licensed. Current versions are source-available under the Screenpipe Commercial License: free for personal, non-profit, educational, and research use, while business use needs a paid license. LokalBot is GPLv3, so anyone can use it at work, study it, and share changes.
- **Q: Does LokalBot record my screen all the time?** No. Out of the box it saves the app name and window title. Visible text and encrypted screenshots are separate opt-ins (on a Mac, they need Accessibility and Screen Recording permission), and captures are deleted after 14 days by default.
- **Q: Can AI agents read my LokalBot history?** Yes, if you allow it. The bundled CLI and MCP server are read-only and stay off until you allow them in Settings > External Agents on a Mac, or Settings > Privacy & Data on Windows and Linux.

### LokalBot vs Rewind / Limitless (https://www.lokalbot.com/lokalbot-vs-rewind · verified 2026-11-20)

Rewind pioneered “search everything you've seen on your Mac” before rebranding to Limitless. After Meta acquired Limitless in December 2025, the Mac app disabled screen and audio capture on December 19, 2025, Limitless stopped selling its Pendant, and rewind.ai now hosts an unrelated site. LokalBot's day timeline carries the local-recall idea forward: smaller, opt-in, GPLv3 open source, and processed on your Mac, Windows, or Linux computer with no cloud backend.

| Feature | LokalBot | Rewind / Limitless (discontinued) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Status | Actively developed | Discontinued: the team moved to Limitless, now part of Meta |
| Screen memory | App and window activity by default; opt-in screen text and encrypted screenshots, searchable by every word | Continuous compressed screen recording, always on |
| Meeting notes | Bot-free microphone + system-audio tracks, summarized locally | Local capture; “Ask Rewind” answers were generated with cloud AI |
| Retention | Deleted after 14 days by default; keeping longer is an explicit opt-in | Grew until you trimmed it yourself |
| Encryption at rest | Screenshots are AES-GCM encrypted on disk | Stored locally on disk |
| Connect AI tools | Read-only CLI and MCP server, off until you turn them on in Settings | None |
| System-wide dictation | Hold ⌥ Space (Alt+Space on Windows and Linux) in any app | No |
| Writing autocomplete | Cotyping (Gemma 4 E2B LokalBot v4), in almost any app (on Linux: X11, or Wayland on Sway, Hyprland, GNOME, and KDE Plasma) | No |
| Source code | Open source, GPLv3 | Proprietary |
| Price | Free | Was subscription-based; no longer purchasable |
| Platforms | macOS 15+ on Apple Silicon; Windows 10/11 x64 and Linux x86_64 in alpha; iOS and Android companion apps | macOS (app no longer available) |

- **Q: Is LokalBot a drop-in Rewind replacement?** Not entirely, and it doesn't try to be. Rewind recorded your screen continuously and let you scrub it like a video. LokalBot tracks app and window activity by default, and adds periodic screenshots with OCR only if you opt in: lighter on disk, easier to reason about, and combined with full meeting capture. You get the search and the timeline, not the video scrubber.
- **Q: What actually happened to Rewind?** The company behind it shifted to Limitless, a wearable pendant with cloud-hosted memory, and stopped developing the Mac app. Meta acquired Limitless in December 2025. A final update turned off Rewind's screen and audio capture on December 19, 2025, and Limitless stopped selling its Pendant. The rewind.ai domain now hosts an unrelated service: the original app is simply gone.
- **Q: How is this different from Windows Recall?** Recall is Windows-only and drew heavy privacy scrutiny. LokalBot runs on the Mac and, in alpha, on Windows, where it's an open-source, opt-in alternative to Recall. Out of the box it logs only which app and window you had open; screen text and screenshots stay off until you turn them on. Screenshots are encrypted at rest, captures are deleted after 14 days by default, and the code that does all of that is open for you to audit.

## Guides & Frequently Asked Questions

### Local AI meeting notes on your Mac (https://www.lokalbot.com/local-ai-meeting-notes-mac)
How local AI meeting notes work on a Mac: bot-free capture, on-device transcription, private summaries, trade-offs, and setup.
- **Q: Can LokalBot work without internet?** Yes, after the app and selected models are downloaded. Built-in transcription, summaries, search, and replay work offline. Update checks, model downloads, and any remote backend you configure need a connection.
- **Q: Does a bot join the meeting?** No. LokalBot records your microphone and the meeting application's system audio on the Mac.
- **Q: Where are meetings stored?** In LokalBot's local Application Support data. They are not copied to a LokalBot account or cloud because neither exists.

### Local AI meeting notes on Linux (https://www.lokalbot.com/local-ai-meeting-notes-linux)
Record, transcribe, and summarize meetings on Linux without a bot or cloud: X11 and Wayland support, apt/dnf/pacman install, and local models.
- **Q: Does LokalBot work on Wayland?** Yes, with limits. Meetings, transcription, notes, search, and Ask work on any desktop. Day memory works on Hyprland, Sway, KDE, and GNOME with the Window Calls extension; screen context needs grim on Sway and Hyprland or the desktop's screenshot portal elsewhere; dictation and selection actions each need a compositor shortcut, bound to lokalbot dictate and lokalbot selection-actions; and autocomplete in other apps works as an input method on Sway, Hyprland, GNOME, and KDE Plasma, but not yet on other compositors.
- **Q: Do I need an NVIDIA GPU?** No. The built-in models run on any Vulkan GPU, including AMD and Intel graphics, or on the CPU. CUDA is an experimental option for NVIDIA GPUs.
- **Q: Can I move my library between Linux and a Mac?** Yes. Both apps read the same library format, and meetings recorded on a Mac play and transcribe on Linux. On Linux the library lives in ~/.local/share/LokalBot. LokalBot doesn't sync it between computers for you.

### Local AI meeting notes on Windows (https://www.lokalbot.com/local-ai-meeting-notes-windows)
Record, transcribe, and summarize Teams, Zoom, and Meet calls on Windows 10/11 without a bot or cloud: per-user install, Vulkan/CUDA, and local models.
- **Q: Why does Windows warn me before LokalBot opens?** The Windows build isn't code-signed yet, so SmartScreen asks first. Choose More info, then Run anyway. The source is public on GitHub, and every update LokalBot installs is checked against its signature first.
- **Q: Does a bot join my Teams or Zoom calls?** No. LokalBot records your microphone and the meeting app's audio, or everything your PC plays when it can't separate the app, on two tracks, so nothing joins the call and other participants don't see a notetaker. Tell them you're recording.
- **Q: Do I need administrator rights?** No. The installer installs LokalBot for your user only. A portable zip that runs from any folder is also available.

### Offline meeting transcription on Mac (https://www.lokalbot.com/offline-meeting-transcription-mac)
Set up offline meeting transcription on Apple Silicon with local speech models, two-track audio, timestamps, and no cloud upload.
- **Q: Will transcription start without Wi-Fi?** Yes, provided the selected model has already finished downloading.
- **Q: Can summaries also run offline?** Yes. Select the built-in llama.cpp backend and a downloaded local model.
- **Q: Which model is smallest?** Among the highlighted speech choices, Qwen3-ASR 0.6B is about 0.7 GB. Actual on-disk usage can change with model packaging.

### Open-source AI meeting notes: what to verify (https://www.lokalbot.com/open-source-ai-meeting-notes)
A checklist for evaluating open-source AI meeting notes: license, local processing, network boundaries, storage, builds, and updates.
- **Q: Is LokalBot free for commercial work?** LokalBot is GPLv3 software, with Autocomplete code ported from Cotabby under AGPLv3, and has no usage subscription. Review the licenses themselves for obligations that apply when you modify or distribute it.
- **Q: Can I audit network access?** Yes. The source is public, and the privacy policy names the normal network paths: models, updates, optional Agent Mode setup, and approved remote inference.
- **Q: Do I need an API key?** No. The built-in local models work without one. API keys are relevant only if you choose an external compatible backend that requires them.

### Record both sides of a Mac meeting without a bot (https://www.lokalbot.com/record-both-sides-mac-meeting-without-bot)
How LokalBot captures your microphone and meeting-app audio as synchronized tracks on macOS without adding a bot participant.
- **Q: Does LokalBot join Zoom or Google Meet?** No. It records the selected app's audio locally through macOS rather than joining as a participant.
- **Q: Can it identify every speaker?** No. It separates microphone audio from the selected app's output, and those sources do not prove identity. Optional diarization can estimate distinct voices within system audio, but accuracy depends on the recording.
- **Q: Is bot-free recording legal everywhere?** No recording method is automatically legal everywhere. You are responsible for notice, consent, workplace rules, and local law.

### Local transcription models for Mac (https://www.lokalbot.com/local-transcription-models-mac)
Compare Granite Speech, Parakeet, Qwen3-ASR, and Whisper for private on-device meeting transcription on Apple Silicon.
- **Q: Which model does LokalBot recommend?** Qwen3-ASR 1.7B has been the default transcription model since LokalBot 0.8.1. You can change it in Settings > Models.
- **Q: Which option covers the most languages?** Whisper large-v3 turbo has the broadest listed coverage at 99 languages. Language count alone does not guarantee the best result for a specific recording.
- **Q: Can I keep several models installed?** Yes. That is useful when your meetings vary by language or audio quality, subject to disk space.

### LokalBot system requirements (https://www.lokalbot.com/system-requirements)
Check LokalBot's requirements on Mac, Windows and Linux (alpha): OS versions, hardware, memory, disk, permissions, and model downloads.
- **Q: Does LokalBot support Intel Macs?** No. Apple Silicon (M1 or later) is required.
- **Q: Does it support macOS 14?** No. The minimum supported version is macOS 15.0.
- **Q: Do I need 32 GB of memory?** No. Smaller models run on lower-memory Apple Silicon Macs and PCs. The 32 GB recommendation applies to the largest local language-model choices.
- **Q: Does it run on Windows on ARM or ARM Linux?** No. The Windows and Linux versions are built only for x64 (x86_64) processors.
- **Q: Can I move my library between a Mac and a PC?** Yes. The Mac, Windows, and Linux apps use the same library format, so a library recorded on one opens on the others. It lives in ~/Library/Application Support/me.dotenv.LokalBot on a Mac, %LOCALAPPDATA%\LokalBot on Windows, and ~/.local/share/LokalBot on Linux.

### Granola and Otter alternatives for Linux and Windows (https://www.lokalbot.com/granola-otter-alternatives-linux-windows)
Granola has no Linux app and caps free Windows history at 30 days. Compare bot-free local note takers for Linux and Windows: LokalBot, OpenWhispr, Meetily.
- **Q: Does Granola work on Linux?** No. Granola ships apps for Mac, Windows, iPhone, and Android. Its web app can view and edit notes but cannot record or transcribe meetings on Linux.
- **Q: What is the best free local Granola alternative for Windows with no 30-day history limit?** LokalBot (GPLv3, alpha) records Teams, Zoom, and Meet audio locally on Windows 10 and 11 with no bot, runs Qwen3-ASR and Qwen3.5 4B LokalBot v4 on Vulkan, CUDA, or CPU, and keeps unlimited meeting history on your disk with no 30-day cutoff.
- **Q: Which open-source apps transcribe locally on Linux?** LokalBot (.deb, .rpm, Arch, .tar.gz) and OpenWhispr (select on-device models during setup) both transcribe locally on Linux. Meetily transcribes locally too, built from source on Linux. Anarlog's Linux beta uses a cloud provider or self-hosted server for transcription. Screenpipe transcribes locally under a source-available commercial license.

### How do I connect meeting notes via MCP to Claude Code, Codex, and Cursor? (https://www.lokalbot.com/claude-code-codex-meeting-notes)
Connect local meeting notes over stdio MCP to Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Windsurf, Gemini CLI, and Antigravity. Read-only, zero cloud bots.
- **Q: Does the MCP server work with Cursor, Windsurf, Gemini CLI, and Antigravity?** Yes. Any MCP client that launches a local stdio server works with command 'lokalbot-cli' and args ['mcp']. That covers Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Windsurf, Gemini CLI, and Antigravity on Mac, Windows, and Linux.
- **Q: Does the agent receive raw meeting audio or screenshots?** No. The MCP server returns text only: meeting metadata, summaries, transcripts, action items, names, cited answers, and (if explicitly enabled) extracted screen text. It never returns audio files or screenshot pixels.
- **Q: Can the MCP server edit or delete my meetings?** No. The read-only MCP server cannot edit or delete meetings. Changing settings or reprocessing a meeting via CLI requires a separate opt-in toggle.

### LokalBot plugins for Claude Code and Codex (https://www.lokalbot.com/claude-code-codex-plugins)
Add LokalBot to Claude Code or Codex to catch up on your work and find what was said in meetings, from a library that stays on your computer.
- **Q: Do I need LokalBot installed?** Yes. The plugins read your library through lokalbot-cli, which comes with LokalBot. The setup skill can install it with you, or you can download it from the LokalBot releases page.
- **Q: Do the plugins cost anything?** No. The plugins and LokalBot are free and open source under GPLv3, and there's no account.
- **Q: Can other agents use LokalBot?** Yes. Install for your coding agent… installs the lokalbot-cli skill for agents that read skills, and any MCP client that can start a local command, such as Cursor, can run lokalbot-cli mcp.

### My company blocks AI notetaker bots. What can I use? (https://www.lokalbot.com/ai-notetaker-bots-blocked-at-work)
Company or client policies blocking Otter, Read.ai, or Fireflies bots? Compare bot-free on-device meeting notes and an IT security approval checklist.
- **Q: Will Teams, Zoom, or Meet show that LokalBot is recording?** No. It doesn't join the call, so the meeting app has no participant to show. That is why telling people is up to you.
- **Q: Is a local recorder allowed if my company bans AI notetakers?** Only if the policy allows it, so ask IT or your manager. A local recorder changes where the data goes, not the fact that people are being recorded.
- **Q: Can IT confirm that meetings never leave the computer?** Yes. The source code is public, and the network test above shows what the app connects to while it records, transcribes, and summarizes with the built-in models.

### Can a bot-free meeting recorder tell who said what? (https://www.lokalbot.com/bot-free-meeting-recorder-speaker-labels)
How a recorder that never joins the call separates speakers, where the names come from, and measured speaker-separation accuracy for LokalBot on Mac.
- **Q: Does LokalBot read participant names from Zoom, Meet, or Teams?** No. It doesn't read the meeting app's participant list or who is speaking. Names come from you, with calendar attendees offered as suggestions.
- **Q: Does speaker separation upload audio?** No. It runs on your computer. The speaker model downloads once on first use. On a Mac with Qwen3-ASR, a word-timing model of about 1 GB downloads too.
- **Q: Can I turn speaker separation off?** Yes. Turn off Separate voices by speaker in Settings > Meetings > Speaker names. Your microphone and the call audio stay on separate tracks either way.

### How do I get meeting transcripts into Obsidian as Markdown? (https://www.lokalbot.com/meeting-transcripts-obsidian-markdown)
Put local meeting transcripts and summaries into an Obsidian vault as Markdown: a note for every meeting, a one-off export, a daily note, or your own script.
- **Q: Is there an Obsidian plugin for LokalBot?** Yes: an open-source LokalBot plugin for Obsidian (github.com/stevyhacker/obsidian-lokalbot) lets you search meetings, sync notes, insert open action items into Daily Notes, and ask LokalBot's local model inside Obsidian. You still don't need a plugin if you only want automatic Markdown note export straight into your vault folder.
- **Q: Do the exported transcripts include speaker names?** Yes. Each transcript line starts with a timestamp and the speaker's name, or a default label such as Me when you haven't named that speaker.
- **Q: Can I use Logseq instead?** Yes, with Logseq OG, which keeps a graph as Markdown files. Meeting notes and the daily note both come in a Logseq format, with page properties and TODO and DONE actions; choose your graph's pages folder for meeting notes. Logseq's newer database version imports Markdown instead of reading a folder, so it won't pick up new notes on its own.

### Best Rewind AI and Limitless Mac alternatives after the Meta shutdown (https://www.lokalbot.com/rewind-limitless-mac-alternatives)
Rewind and Limitless stopped Mac capture after Meta's acquisition. Compare open-source and local Mac screen memory and meeting alternatives in 2026.
- **Q: Is LokalBot an exact video-scrubber clone of Rewind?** No. Rewind recorded continuous compressed screen video so you could scrub frame by frame. LokalBot focuses on searchable activity, opt-in OCR text, AES-GCM encrypted periodic screenshots (14-day default retention), and full bot-free meeting notes. You get fast keyword and semantic search across what you saw and heard without massive video archives.
- **Q: Can LokalBot run if I also switch between Mac and Windows or Linux?** Yes. LokalBot uses the same local SQLite library format across its Apple Silicon Mac app and its Windows and Linux (alpha) Rust + GPUI app.
- **Q: What if I want to replace a Limitless Pendant for in-person meetings?** LokalBot offers free iOS and Android companion apps that record in-person audio and sync end-to-end encrypted over LAN or Tailscale straight to your computer for local transcription, with zero cloud subscription. See LokalBot vs Plaud for details.

### An open-source Windows Recall alternative that is opt-in and encrypted (https://www.lokalbot.com/open-source-windows-recall-alternative)
Want searchable screen and meeting memory on Windows without Microsoft Recall or Copilot+ NPU lock-in? Compare LokalBot's opt-in, encrypted Rust app.
- **Q: Do I need a Copilot+ PC or an NPU to run LokalBot on Windows?** No. LokalBot runs on any Windows 10 or 11 x64 machine using any Vulkan GPU (AMD, Intel, or NVIDIA), experimental CUDA on NVIDIA GPUs, or the CPU.
- **Q: Does LokalBot take screenshots immediately after install?** No. Fresh installs record app and window activity only. Reading screen text and saving AES-GCM encrypted screenshots are explicit opt-in toggles in Settings.
- **Q: How does LokalBot compare to Screenpipe on Windows?** Screenpipe records screen and audio continuously (~30 GB/mo) under a source-available commercial license. LokalBot starts activity-only, deletes captures after 14 days by default, ships built-in local summary models, and is free under GPLv3. See LokalBot vs Screenpipe.

### GDPR AI meeting notes with zero cloud subprocessors (https://www.lokalbot.com/gdpr-local-ai-meeting-notes)
Run GDPR-friendly AI meeting notes with zero cloud subprocessors, no DPA chain, and no bots. Compare on-device tools and participant consent rules.
- **Q: Do I need a Data Processing Agreement (DPA) to use LokalBot?** When you run LokalBot with its built-in local models, no meeting data is sent to the LokalBot project or any hosted service, so there is no LokalBot cloud processor handling your personal data. If you opt into an external API or cloud plan in Settings, you need a DPA with that provider.
- **Q: Is bot-free local recording automatically legal under GDPR?** No. GDPR requires a lawful basis (often explicit consent) and clear notice to every participant before recording a call, regardless of whether a bot joins or the audio stays on your laptop.
- **Q: How does LokalBot compare to European cloud notetakers like Jamie?** Jamie hosts notes on EU servers in Frankfurt and deletes raw audio after transcription, which still requires trusting cloud servers and paying EUR 24-47/mo. LokalBot processes and stores everything on your own device for free under GPLv3. See LokalBot vs Jamie.

### Best local and open-source AI meeting note takers (2026) (https://www.lokalbot.com/best-local-ai-meeting-notes)
Compare 6 local AI meeting note takers in 2026: LokalBot, Meetily, Anarlog, OpenWhispr, MacWhisper, and Screenpipe on local WER, RAM, platforms, and license.
- **Q: What is the best completely free, open-source local AI meeting note taker?** LokalBot (GPLv3) ships every feature in one free app with no paid tier: bot-free two-track capture, fine-tuned Apache-2.0 local models for transcription and summaries, speaker separation, Obsidian export, and a free read-only local MCP server. Meetily Community Edition (MIT) is also free for core local recording and summaries, with speaker separation and MCP in its paid Pro tier.
- **Q: Do local AI meeting note takers work completely offline?** Yes, once the speech and language models are downloaded. LokalBot, Meetily Community Edition, and MacWhisper transcribe offline. In OpenWhispr, choose on-device models during setup instead of its recommended cloud option. Anarlog transcribes locally on supported Macs and pairs with Ollama or LM Studio for offline summaries.
- **Q: How much RAM do I need for local meeting transcription and summaries?** A 16 GB Apple Silicon Mac or a 16 GB Windows or Linux PC comfortably runs a 0.6B-1.7B speech model (1.0-2.5 GB) and a 4B quantized summary model (~2.7 GB) sequentially. On 8 GB machines, use compact speech models like Qwen3-ASR 0.6B or Parakeet 0.6B and smaller summarizers. Check your exact hardware at lokalbot.com/hardware.
- **Q: Which local meeting note takers run on Linux and Windows?** LokalBot (native Rust + GPUI alpha with .deb, .rpm, Arch, and Windows installer), OpenWhispr (AppImage, .deb, .rpm, Windows), Screenpipe (AppImage, Windows), and Anarlog (beta; cloud or BYO transcription server on Linux/Windows). Meetily ships native Windows binaries and builds from source on Linux. MacWhisper is macOS and iOS only.
- **Q: Which local meeting note taker has a free local MCP server for Claude Code or Cursor?** LokalBot includes a free, read-only local stdio MCP server (lokalbot-cli mcp, off until enabled in Settings) with no cloud sync required. Anarlog and Screenpipe also expose local MCP servers. Meetily gates MCP to Pro, and OpenWhispr's MCP server is hosted on paid plans.

### The best open-source AI assistants you can run locally (https://www.lokalbot.com/best-open-source-ai-assistants)
Ollama, LM Studio, Jan, AnythingLLM, Open WebUI, and LokalBot compared on memory, document chat, licenses, platforms, and setup, with real screenshots.
- **Q: What is the best local AI assistant?** It depends on the job. For a private ChatGPT-style chat, Jan (open source) or LM Studio (more polished, but closed source). To run models for other apps and agents, Ollama. To ask questions across your documents, AnythingLLM. For one web app shared by a household or team, Open WebUI. For an assistant that remembers your meetings and what you saw on screen, LokalBot.
- **Q: Which local AI assistant has memory like ChatGPT?** Open WebUI has a Memory feature, marked experimental, where you or the model can save facts about you. AnythingLLM has Memories, off by default, which it extracts from recent chats every three hours. LokalBot remembers your meetings and, if you turn it on, your screen, and learns facts and preferences from your own words. Ollama and LM Studio have no memory, and Jan lists it as coming soon.
- **Q: Is LM Studio open source?** No. The LM Studio app is proprietary, though free for home and work since July 2025. Its lms command-line tool, its SDKs, and its MLX engine are open source under the MIT license.
- **Q: Is Open WebUI still open source?** Its code is public, but since version 0.6.6 (April 2025) it uses the Open WebUI License, which adds a branding clause to BSD-3 terms. Its own documentation says it is not an OSI-approved open-source license. Code up to version 0.6.5 remains BSD-3.
- **Q: Do I need a GPU to run a local AI assistant?** No. Our test machine had none, and a 4B model answered at about 12 to 20 tokens a second on an 8-core CPU, which is readable but not fast. A recent GPU or an Apple Silicon Mac is much faster and can run larger, more capable models.
- **Q: Can these assistants work completely offline?** Yes, once the app and a model are downloaded, local chat works offline in all six. Some features use the network by default: Ollama's cloud models and web search, Jan's web search, AnythingLLM's anonymous telemetry, and update checks in most apps. Each app's section on this page says what to switch off.
